title: The Applause for Nobody in Particular
skyStory: The gibbous moon, ninety percent lit, is still basking in Leo, almost full and very aware of it. It has started signing autographs for passing comets. Spring is two days away and the moon is warming up for its big performance on Joel's birthday. Somewhere a snowdrop has pushed through the mud and is bowing to an empty theatre.

reading: Two days from your birthday, the universe starts dropping hints. A song you love on the radio. A stranger holding a door. A warm breeze where there should be cold. Each one is a little drumroll for Sunday. Count them.

Here is the brave thing: today, let someone do something nice for you without trying to repay it immediately. The [[Six of Pentacles]] has been working on you for months. This is the dress rehearsal. Somebody will offer help, a treat, or a compliment. Say yes. Say thank you. Then stop talking, which is the hardest part. The cabin believes in you.
joel.mission: Accept one offer of help today without saying you do not need to, then actually let them help.
joel.omen: A snowdrop or first green shoot poking through dirt. It means something small and brave is about to bloom in you.

reading: The Wood Rat has a secret project: something for Joel's birthday, even if it is only a message. Today the Leo moon makes your creativity bold. Whatever you have planned, make it a little bigger, a little brighter, a little more ridiculous.

Around 4 pm, the light will hit your diamond and throw sparkles across your desk or table. Take that as a sign that whatever you are making is exactly right. You are clever, you see what others miss, and you have been collecting tiny details about Joel all year. Use one. The specific one. He will notice it, and his reaction will be worth everything.
nancy.mission: Write down one small, specific detail you know about Joel that nobody else would remember, and save it for Sunday.
nancy.omen: Sparkles of light thrown by a ring or glass. It means your creative instinct is perfectly on target right now.

together.text: Birthday countdown begins. Each of you name one thing you are brave enough to do this weekend that you would not have done a year ago. Send it in one sentence. The moon is nearly full and keeps track of promises.

game.intro: Applause for nobody in particular! Now give the crew a sound actually worth clapping for.
game.prompt: A tiny crowd: one person cheering, a polite little clap, a single kazoo in the back row.
